rows.proof_boundary: All integrals start at 1; beta=(1+alpha)/2 and lambda=(1-alpha)/2.
rows.statement: For 0<alpha<1 define M(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n), A_alpha(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)n^(-alpha), I_alpha=int M(x)^2*x^(-2-alpha)dx, and J_alpha=int A_alpha(x)^2*x^(alpha-2)dx.

rows.proof_boundary: Stieltjes integration by parts; no zero-free region is used.
rows.statement: A_alpha(x)=x^(-alpha)M(x)+alpha*int_1^x M(u)u^(-alpha-1)du.

rows.proof_boundary: The inverse Stieltjes identity for mu(n)=n^alpha [mu(n)n^(-alpha)].
rows.statement: M(x)=x^alpha*A_alpha(x)-alpha*int_1^x A_alpha(u)u^(alpha-1)du.

rows.proof_boundary: A unitary logarithmic change of variables on t>=0.
rows.statement: For x=e^t put m(t)=e^(-beta*t)M(e^t) and a(t)=e^(-lambda*t)A_alpha(e^t); then ||m||_2^2=I_alpha and ||a||_2^2=J_alpha.

rows.proof_boundary: Equation 2 in logarithmic coordinates.
rows.statement: a=m+alpha*V_lambda*m, where V_c f(t)=int_0^t exp(-c(t-u))f(u)du.

rows.proof_boundary: Equation 3 in logarithmic coordinates.
rows.statement: m=a-alpha*V_beta*a.

rows.proof_boundary: The forward Fourier multiplier is (beta+it)/(lambda+it), whose modulus lies in [1,beta/lambda].
rows.statement: I_alpha<=J_alpha<=((1+alpha)/(1-alpha))^2*I_alpha.

rows.proof_boundary: Interchange the finite-prefix step function and the integral.
rows.statement: int_1^infinity A_alpha(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/[s*zeta(s+alpha)] initially for Re(s)>1-alpha.

rows.proof_boundary: Hardy-space continuation from the initial half-plane; finiteness excludes a reciprocal-zeta pole on the boundary.
rows.statement: If the energies are finite, Mellin-Plancherel writes J_alpha with denominator lambda^2+t^2 and I_alpha with denominator beta^2+t^2 against the same |zeta(beta+it)|^(-2).

rows.proof_boundary: The same reciprocal-zeta boundary data appear in both coordinates; only a scalar Hardy multiplier changes.
rows.statement: J_alpha=(1/(2pi))*int_R dt/[(lambda^2+t^2)|zeta(beta+it)|^2], while I_alpha has beta^2+t^2 in the first factor.

rows.proof_boundary: A_alpha(x)=A_alpha(k) on every half-open cell [k,k+1).
rows.statement: J_alpha=(1/(1-alpha))*sum_(k>=1)A_alpha(k)^2*[k^(alpha-1)-(k+1)^(alpha-1)].

rows.proof_boundary: Compare x^(alpha-2) on each unit cell.
rows.statement: For E_alpha=sum k^(alpha-2)A_alpha(k)^2, 2^(alpha-2)E_alpha<=J_alpha<=E_alpha.

rows.proof_boundary: The companion unit-cell comparison in the Mertens coordinate.
rows.statement: For M_alpha=sum M(k)^2/k^(2+alpha), 2^(-2-alpha)M_alpha<=I_alpha<=M_alpha.

rows.proof_boundary: Rows 7, 12, and 13; the constants are explicit and nonsharp only because of unit-cell comparison.
rows.statement: 2^(-2-alpha)M_alpha<=E_alpha<=2^(2-alpha)*((1+alpha)/(1-alpha))^2*M_alpha.

rows.proof_boundary: Compose row 14 with the already checked cofinal OU/Mertens criterion; this is an equivalent target, not a proof.
rows.statement: RH iff E_(alpha_j)<infinity for every member of any fixed cofinal sequence alpha_j->0 in (0,1).

rows.proof_boundary: No normalization or deleted weight is hidden in the comparison.
rows.statement: With alpha=2omega, A_alpha(k) is exactly the weighted Mobius prefix M_alpha(k) used in the Burnol tail-discrepancy reduction.

rows.proof_boundary: Every omitted divisor satisfies N<d<=k and hence floor(k/d)=1.
rows.statement: For N<k<=2N, H_(omega,N)(k)=A_alpha(k)-A_alpha(N).

rows.proof_boundary: Insert row 17 into the exact finite-tail discrepancy.
rows.statement: For N<k<=2N, D_(omega,N)(k)=A_alpha(k)-A_alpha(N)-k*r_(omega,N).

rows.proof_boundary: Discrete Abel summation; A_alpha(n)/n->0 follows unconditionally from alpha>0.
rows.statement: r_(omega,N)=-A_alpha(N)/(N+1)+sum_(n>N)A_alpha(n)/(n(n+1)).

rows.proof_boundary: Dyadic comparison for the decreasing weight k^(alpha-2).
rows.statement: If V_N=sum_(N<k<=2N)|D_N(k)|^2 and E_D=sum k^(alpha-2)|D_N(k)|^2, then 2^(alpha-2)N^(alpha-2)V_N<=E_D<=N^(alpha-2)V_N.

rows.proof_boundary: The Gram determinant W_0*W_2-W_1^2 is strictly positive.
rows.statement: For W_q=sum_(N<k<=2N)k^(alpha-2+q), the weighted energy of A_alpha(N)+k*r_N is A_alpha(N)^2*W_0+2A_alpha(N)r_N*W_1+r_N^2*W_2.

rows.proof_boundary: Weighted triangle inequality plus W_0<=N^(alpha-1) and W_2<=2^alpha*N^(1+alpha).
The first q-block is a high-pass observation with one unobserved constant anchor mode.
rows.statement: Adding a constant C to A_alpha(N) and every A_alpha(k) on N<k<=2N leaves D_N(k) unchanged when r_N is fixed.

rows.proof_boundary: This is an operator countermodel, not a surrogate for mu; it proves that post-prefix residual and tail data alone cannot bound the absolute weighted-prefix block.
rows.statement: For any finitely supported coefficient sequence whose prefix is the nonzero constant C after N, r_N=0 and D_N(k)=0 for all k>N, but F_alpha(N)=C^2*W_0>0.

rows.proof_boundary: The constant-tail countermodel has r_N=0 and arbitrary anchor.
rows.statement: Even the forced rate r_N=O(N^(-(1+alpha)/2)) does not control N^(alpha-1)A_alpha(N)^2 without an additional anchor theorem.

rows.proof_boundary: Reorder the triangle by the larger index n=m+h.
rows.statement: sum_(h<X)sum_(Y<=X-h)C_h(Y)=sum_(n=2)^X (X-n+1)mu(n)M(n-1).

rows.proof_boundary: The one-dimensional collapse is exact but still contains the unknown Mertens prefix endogenously.
rows.statement: M(n)^2-M(n-1)^2=2mu(n)M(n-1)+mu(n)^2, and triangular summation of this identity recovers sum_(k<=X)M(k)^2.

rows.proof_boundary: Only the published algebraic identity is imported; its bounded-test estimates are not promoted to the endogenous test.
rows.statement: Green and Tao, Lemma 4.1, give Vaughan's exact Type I/II decomposition for sums of mu(n)f(n) on a dyadic interval.

rows.proof_boundary: Finite divisor reindexing; independently checked for arbitrary finite test vectors.
rows.statement: For 1<=U,V<=N, sum_(N<n<=2N)mu(n)f(n)=-TI(f)+TII(f), with a_d=sum_(bc=d,b<=U,c<=V)mu(b)mu(c) and b_d=sum_(c|d,c>V)mu(c).

rows.proof_boundary: The inverse theorem for a bounded external f cannot be quoted without retaining the Mertens dependence.
rows.statement: After row 26 the Vaughan test is f_X(n)=(X-n+1)M(n-1), not an exogenous bounded function.

rows.proof_boundary: No small absorbable coefficient is supplied by the identity alone; logarithmic Mobius orthogonality is one power short.
rows.statement: sum_(n<=X)|f_X(n)|^2<=X^2*sum_(k<=X)M(k)^2, so generic Cauchy-Schwarz in the Type I/II forms recycles the target energy on the right-hand side.

rows.proof_boundary: The explicit aggregate avoids the endogenous-test defect, but no O_epsilon(X^(2+epsilon)) estimate for -TI_X+TII_X is asserted.
rows.statement: Before collapsing h and Y, Vaughan applies with the bounded test f_(h,Y)(m)=mu(m+h)1_(m<=Y) on each dyadic m-block, giving T(X)=B_1(X)-TI_X+TII_X exactly.

rows.proof_boundary: Post-prefix V_N and the reciprocal-tail rate do not supply it.
rows.statement: Control the constant anchor mode N^((alpha-1)/2)A_alpha(N) in a summable dyadic theorem, using the limiting Burnol energy or another arithmetic input.

rows.proof_boundary: This is the live noncircular bilinear handoff; no RH, PF-infinity, or Lambda<=0 conclusion is recorded.
rows.statement: Prove an O_epsilon(X^(2+epsilon)) signed aggregate estimate for the pre-collapse Vaughan Type I/II forms over h and Y, without rowwise absolute values or RH.

status: exact weighted-prefix, first-block affine-defect, and Vaughan handoff reduction with two open arithmetic gates
